Hi Jane —

Thanks again for the time on Friday. Attached is our second-pass redline for the pilot order form (Acme_OrderForm_v2_redline.docx) and a quick two-sheet comparing the Order Form term mechanics to the MSA baseline (MSA-term-comparison.xlsx). Two items we want to reconcile before we send anything to procurement/legal on your side:

1) Notice window mismatch: Your draft has a 30-day auto-renew notice for pilot accounts, while the MSA references a 60-day notice for non-pilot commercial accounts. For operational predictability we prefer to keep the pilot at 60 days (align with billing cadence) but are open to a limited carveout if Acme needs runway.

2) Termination for convenience (TFC) "soft exit": The Order Form attempts to add a narrow TFC that lets Acme decommission services without breaking integrations, with a 45-day transition and prorated credits. Legal flagged this as potentially open-ended. We want to propose a capped TFC remedy that preserves our offboarding work and limits post-termination liabilities.

Can you confirm who at Acme (procurement vs legal) we should coordinate the final language with? If useful, I can propose draft clause language that trades off a 60-day notice in exchange for a hard cap on TFC credits.

Attachments: Acme_OrderForm_v2_redline.docx (redline), MSA-term-comparison.xlsx (comparison chart)

Looping you both in for legal/offer strategy. Jane pushed Harrison from Acme legal onto clause negotiation. Two asks:

1) Laura — can you draft a tight TFC clause we can offer that:
   - Confines credits to pro-rated prepaid amounts AND a single termination fee (formula below),

Marcus / Ben —

Draft clause below is what I recommend sending to Harrison as our first pass. It aims to be operationally clear, limits financial exposure, and gives Acme a prompt runway for pilots. Please flag anything that materially impacts delivery or revenue recognition.

--- Proposed TFC clause (first-pass) ---
1. Termination for Convenience (Pilot Order Form only): Either party may terminate the Pilot Order Form upon written notice to the other party. Termination shall become effective 45 days after the recipient of notice ("Transition Period") to allow for orderly offboarding.

2. Financial Remedies: Upon termination under this Section, Customer will be entitled only to: (a) a pro rata refund of any prepaid but unused fees for the remainder of the then-current billing period, and (b) a single termination fee equal to the lesser of (i) one (1) times the Customer's average monthly spend for the three (3) months preceding termination and (ii) twenty percent (20%) of the remaining value of the Order Form at the time of termination, not to exceed fifty thousand U.S. dollars (USD 50,000).

3. Sunset and Scope: Any pilot-specific termination concessions will automatically expire twelve (12) months after the Effective Date of the Pilot Order Form or upon completion of the Pilot (whichever is earlier). Following expiration, termination rights will be governed by the MSA.

4. No Continuing Obligations: Except for the activities required during the Transition Period and obligations expressly set forth in this Agreement, neither party shall have continuing obligations to the other after the effective date of termination.

--- end clause ---

Negotiation posture: offer this clause in exchange for Acme accepting a 60-day notice for pilot termination, or alternatively allow 30-day notice if Acme accepts the termination fee cap and sunset language.

Ben — operational callouts: if we accept 30-day notice we should ensure the Transition Period still remains 45 days (i.e., notice triggers 45-day offboarding window; pilot notice is about billing trigger). If that creates scheduling issues, say so and propose a counter.

Happy to hop on a quick legal-to-legal call; I can be available Thursday 10:00–11:00 PT.

Best,
Laura Bennett
